title: dianthus fimbriatus var. macrophyllus
intro: Dianthus fimbriatus var. macrophyllus, commonly known as the fringed pink, is a type of flowering plant in the carnation family (Caryophyllaceae). It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, helping to soothe skin irritations and protect against cell damage. The therapeutic actions of the fringed pink include acting as a demulcent, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant, making it useful for wound healing and skin care. The bioactive constituents of the plant are primarily flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
